import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter to expression and clinical features only
    expr_clin_ids = [fid for fid, typ in zip(feats.ids, feats.types) if typ in ('expression', 'clinical')]
    
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effects = []
    for fid in expr_clin_ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        
        # Effect size: difference in means between groups
        mean_y1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        effect_size = mean_y1 - mean_y0
        
        # Welch's t-test
        group0 = x[y == 0]
        group1 = x[y == 1]
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
        
        effects.append((fid, effect_size, abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (absolute) and p-value
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: (-abs(x[1]), x[3]))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated features)
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for a, b, r in [(a, b, r) for a, b, r in [
        ("JMP13", "UCZK18P", 0.91), ("NUPL12", "UCZK18P", -0.90), ("UCZK18P", "YDWW2P", -0.89),
        ("RWS18B", "UCZK18P", 0.88), ("EWS12P", "NUPL12", 0.87), ("YYB16", "RWS18B", -0.83),
        ("YYB16", "UCZK18P", -0.82), ("JMP13", "NUPL12", -0.81), ("NUPL12", "YDWW2P", 0.81),
        ("RWS18B", "NUPL12", -0.80), ("UCZK18P", "YHA15", -0.80), ("SYA1", "IRI7", 0.80),
        ("UCZK18P", "WCWI4P", -0.79), ("JMP13", "YDWW2P", -0.79), ("JMP13", "RWS18B", 0.79),
        ("BTF13L", "UCZK18P", -0.79), ("UCZK18P", "IRI7", 0.78), ("AGMM3", "ZFZ18", 0.78),
        ("AGMM3", "JZT12", 0.77), ("JMP13", "VOO6", 0.77)
    ] if abs(r) >= 0.6]:
        correlated_pairs.add((a, b))
    
    # Build a graph of correlations to identify clusters
    adj_list = defaultdict(set)
    for a, b in correlated_pairs:
        adj_list[a].add(b)
        adj_list[b].add(a)
    
    # Remove duplicates by keeping highest-effect feature in each cluster
    seen = set()
    unique_features = []
    for fid, _, _, _ in effects:
        if fid in seen:
            continue
        # Check if this feature is part of any correlation cluster
        cluster = set([fid])
        stack = [fid]
        while stack:
            current = stack.pop()
            for neighbor in adj_list[current]:
                if neighbor not in cluster:
                    cluster.add(neighbor)
                    stack.append(neighbor)
        # Add the best feature from this cluster
        cluster_features = [f for f in cluster if f in expr_clin_ids]
        max_effect = -float('inf')
        best_fid = None
        for f in cluster_features:
            for fid_e, effect, _, _ in effects:
                if fid_e == f and effect > max_effect:
                    max_effect = effect
                    best_fid = f
        if best_fid:
            unique_features.append(best_fid)
        seen.update(cluster)
    
    # Select top candidates for drivers
    top_candidates = [fid for fid, _, _, _ in effects[:10]]
    selected_drivers = []
    for fid in top_candidates:
        if fid in unique_features:
            selected_drivers.append(fid)
        if len(selected_drivers) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
            break
    
    # Limit to at most 4 drivers
    selected_drivers = selected_drivers[:4]
    
    # For products, look for significant interactions among top features
    products = []
    top_feature_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_drivers if fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Simple approach: check pairwise products of top features
    for i in range(len(top_feature_indices)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_feature_indices)):
            idx1, idx2 = top_feature_indices[i], top_feature_indices[j]
            prod_col = feats.x[:, idx1] * feats.x[:, idx2]
            auc = roc_auc_score(feats.y, prod_col)
            if auc > 0.55:  # Only include strong products
                products.append((selected_drivers[i], selected_drivers[j]))
    
    # Loadings: use standardized coefficients from a simple regression
    if selected_drivers:
        cols = [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_drivers if fid in feats.ids]
        X = feats.x[:, cols]
        model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear')
        model.fit(X, feats.y)
        loadings = dict(zip(selected_drivers, model.coef_[0]))
    else:
        loadings = {}
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(selected_drivers),
        columns=tuple(expr_clin_ids),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
